entries.test: Tesla's publicly documented driving capabilities and driver-supervision requirements as of January 2024 would establish whether every new Tesla could drive itself.
entries.note: The promise is attributed to Musk, but the assertion that it remains unfulfilled is Zitron's own.

entries.test: Public deployment records, safety data, and regulatory findings would establish whether autonomous taxis could safely operate on public roads in January 2024 or achieved that capability only years later.
entries.note: The forecast is anchored to January 2024; evidence covering the intervening years is now available. The wording gives no precise safety threshold.

entries.test: Archived popular internet home pages from around January 2024, together with factual and provenance checks of their content, would establish whether AI-generated misinformation was prevalent.
entries.note: “Full of” states substantial prevalence, although no numerical threshold is supplied.

entries.test: Software vendors' public AI announcements, product plans, releases, and accompanying explanations around January 2024 would show how widespread AI adoption plans were and whether vendors explained user benefits.
entries.note: “Wants to add” describes an apparent intention or trend; “is adding” strengthens it into implementation. “Seemingly every” qualifies the breadth of the observation.
